questions.question: OP-01/O71 (readinto1, readlines): D70 adopts io.BufferedIOBase's contract, which also has readinto1 and readlines, both drawing from the position; D93's data-read list and D101 name neither. What do they do?

options.label: Both, io semantics (Recommended)
options.description: readinto1(b) writes 1 to min(len(b), r) bytes in at most one backend request, 0 at the end (as read1); readlines(hint=-1) returns readline() results until the end, stopping once their total reaches hint > 0. Both join D93's data-read list (so Failed raises again, D18's column), coroutines on the async form; NP9's scope gains readlines without a positive hint. Source: io.BufferedIOBase, io.IOBase.readlines.

options.label: Neither offered
options.description: D70 narrowed to the methods it lists; readinto1 and readlines raise AttributeError. Code that calls them on a BufferedIOBase (rare) breaks; D70's adopted option is withdrawn in part.

questions.question: OP-01/O71 (io's other six): writable, flush, fileno, isatty, writelines, detach are io.IOBase/BufferedIOBase methods no decision names. What does each do, and in which async form?

options.label: io defaults, plain (Recommended)
options.description: writable() and isatty() False, flush() a no-op; fileno(), writelines() and detach() raise io.UnsupportedOperation. All plain methods in the async form (no request, D101's rule). On a Closed stream each raises ValueError (D117); on a Failed one they answer as on an Open one (D93's tell). Source: io.IOBase, io.BufferedIOBase defaults for a non-seekable read-only object.

options.label: Only writable, isatty
options.description: writable() and isatty() False; flush, fileno, writelines and detach not offered (AttributeError). Smaller surface, but wrappers that call flush() on close (TextIOWrapper does) or probe fileno() break. Source: unsourced.

questions.question: OP-01/O71 (where listed): D100 makes D93 the one list of data reads, but D101 enumerates them again for the async form. Where are the data reads listed?

options.label: D93 only, D101 by rule (Recommended)
options.description: D101 reads: every data read (D93's list) and close() are coroutines, line iteration and chunks async iterators, every other method plain. Adding a data read then changes one list. D101 and D114's restatement amended. Source: D100's reason.

options.label: Both lists, kept in step
options.description: D101 keeps its enumeration, gaining readinto1 and readlines alongside D93; two lists a later amendment must both reach, D100's reason not applied to the async form.
